chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'My wife made it upon herself the fasting of two months. She gave birth to her child, and pregnancy overtook her, so she was not strong enough for the fasting.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Let her give in charity, in place of each day, a Mudd for a poor person.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a woman who cannot fast due to pregnancy and childbirth after making a vow?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a woman who vows to fast for two consecutive months but is exempted due to the physical hardship of childbirth and immediate subsequent pregnancy. Unlike the general rule of making up missed days (qada), the Imam (peace be upon him) prescribes feeding a poor person a Mudd for each day, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on alleviating hardship (rukhas) in vow fulfillment. This ruling underscores the distinction between obligatory fasting and voluntary vows, where the inability to fast due to valid excuses shifts the compensation towards charity rather than repetition.
